notes.text: Kailer Yamamoto is day to day (upper body injury) and missed their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters.

John Marino is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and has missed the last 5 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Andrew Peeke has taken his spot beside Nate Schmidt. That pair has had 55% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 59:05 together, about what it had with Marino (59%).
Michael Carcone has not dressed for the last 9 games.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 28% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the fourth-lowest in the league (a typical team: 43%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Owen Tippett has not dressed for the last 6 games. He is a top-six forward.
Rasmus Ristolainen is on injured reserve and has missed the last 2 games. Jamie Drysdale has taken his spot beside Travis Sanheim.

PHI.head: The Flyers have a hill to climb
PHI.body: Even though Philadelphia has home-ice advantage and Utah will be without Marino, the Mammoth have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Flyers can pull it off if their power play gets going.

story.head: Who drives the play: the Mammoth
paras: The Flyers are winless in three (0-2-1), while the Mammoth (9-5-0) beat Pittsburgh 4-3 in overtime on Thursday. Going in, the Mammoth are second in the Central (tied for eighth in the NHL) and the Flyers last in the Metropolitan (tied for 28th).

The Mammoth have played better than their record (.643) says: their chances are worth about .737, and their goaltending has held them back. The Flyers’ record (.333) is about what their chances are worth.

The Mammoth roll their lines more evenly than anyone (1st), rarely get pinned in their own end (1st) and let the point shots come and guard the net (2nd). As for the Flyers, they play slow, tight games (2nd lowest), pick their shots (3rd lowest) and get a lot of their shots blocked (30th). Philadelphia has scored 1.93 goals a game, the fewest in the league. The Mammoth are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Flyers. Beyond that, both teams like to hit, so expect plenty of it.

Clayton Keller (4 G / 12 A / 16 P in 14 GP) leads the Mammoth in scoring, with a point in five straight games against Philadelphia. Logan Cooley (7 G / 8 A / 15 P in 14 GP) has a team-high seven goals, with seven points in his last five games. For the Flyers, Trevor Zegras (4 G / 9 A / 13 P in 15 GP) leads the way in scoring, with nine points in his last five games. Matvei Michkov (9 G / 2 A / 11 P in 15 GP) has a team-high nine goals, tied for ninth in the NHL.

Karel Vejmelka (6-4-0 / .877 SV% in 10 GS) will likely start for Utah. Philadelphia has two options in net: Joseph Woll (1-5-2 / .899 SV% in 8 GS) and Dan Vladař (2-3-2 / .888 SV% in 7 GS). They have split the last ten starts, and Woll got the last one on Wednesday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.

At home, Rick Tocchet likes to send Zegras, Dvorak and Knuble out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Keller, Schmaltz and Guenther. One more thing: the Mammoth usually control more of the chances than the Flyers do.
